name: California Poppy
grown_as: A hardy annual from the seed mix 'Californian Superb Mix': orange, yellow, cream, pink, scarlet and red. Drawn in the typical orange. ⚠️ CHECK the colour William wants drawn.
habit: A low, loose, sprawling mound 20 to 30 cm tall and 20 to 30 cm across of feathery blue-grey leaves, with flowers held just above on bare stalks.

leaf.arrangement: Mostly from the base, a few alternate up the stems
leaf.type: Finely divided two or three times into many narrow segments, feathery like a carrot leaf
leaf.outline: Triangular to oval overall, 5 to 15 cm long including the stalk
leaf.base: The stalk widens a little where it meets the stem
leaf.tip: Each segment narrow, ending blunt or in a small point
leaf.margin: Smooth: the segments themselves are the cut
leaf.veins: One fine vein in each segment

flower.form: A silky cup opening to a saucer, closing at night and in dull weather
flower.colour: Bright orange, deeper at the base (mix: also yellow, cream, pink and red)
flower.centre: Many orange-yellow stamens around a slender style
flower.behind: A flat, pinkish rim (the swollen top of the stalk) under the petals. The sepals form a pointed pale cap over the bud that is pushed off as it opens.
flower.carried: Alone on long bare stalks, facing up

fruit: A long, thin, ribbed pod 5 to 8 cm, straight or slightly curved, held up on the stalk; green ripening pale brown and splitting with a snap. Seeds round, about 1.5 mm, grey-brown, finely netted.
seedling: Two long, narrow, grey-green seed leaves, each split into two at the tip, then small feathery true leaves
winter: None: grown as an annual. Autumn-sown seedlings sit over winter as small grey feathery tufts.

leaf: leaf finely cut into many narrow segments, feathery
bloom: four broad silky orange petals in a cup
a flat pinkish rim under the petals
seedling: two long narrow seed leaves split at the tips
young: a low mound of feathery blue-grey leaves
flower: a low sprawling mound of blue-grey feathery leaves
orange cup-shaped flowers held alone on bare stalks above
seedhead: long, thin, ribbed pods standing up from the mound

look_alikes: Welsh poppy (Papaver cambricum) is yellow or orange with broader, greener leaves and a nodding bud. Common poppy has bristly leaves and a round seed box. Marigolds have daisy flowers.
